name: Tabby
official_status_notes: Self-hosted AI coding assistant (Apache-2.0); code completion server you run yourself; supports CPU inference. Verify recent releases.
best_for: Teams that need an in-house autocomplete server with data privacy.
weaknesses: Autocomplete/chat focus; not an autonomous agent.
hardware_requirements: Depends on model; smaller models work on CPU.

name: Ollama
official_status_notes: Local model runner: one-command model management and an OpenAI-compatible local API (localhost:11434); runs GGUF models on CPU or GPU; the de-facto local backend behind BYOK tools (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source; no API costs for local models.
best_for: The easiest way to run local models (3Bâ€“8B class) on modest hardware; pairs with Cline, Continue, Aider, Twinny, and more.
strengths: Dead-simple model pulls; OpenAI-compatible local API; wide tool support.
weaknesses: No agent features of its own; CPU-only 8 GB machines are limited to 3Bâ€“8B class models at usable speeds.
hardware_requirements: 3B models ~3 GB RAM; 7â€“8B Q4 ~5â€“6 GB; 14B+ impractical on 8 GB CPU-only.

name: llama.cpp
official_status_notes: The reference C/C++ engine for local LLM inference: CPU-first, GGUF quantization, llama-server with an OpenAI-compatible API; the foundation beneath Ollama and GPT4All (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source; runs on your own hardware.
best_for: Lowest-level local inference engine for quantized GGUF models on CPU; for builders who want control, not polish.
strengths: CPU-first; quantization; OpenAI-compatible llama-server; huge ecosystem.
weaknesses: Manual setup and model management; not an agent or assistant by itself.
hardware_requirements: Runs on CPU; RAM â‰ˆ model size + overhead.

name: LM Studio
official_status_notes: Proprietary (free) desktop app for discovering and running local LLMs (MLX + llama.cpp runtimes) on Windows/macOS/Linux; includes SDKs and the `lms` CLI; new 'Bionic' agent layer (verified Sep 2026).
license: Proprietary (free for personal use â€” verify current terms)
pricing_summary: Free download for personal use; verify licensing for other uses.
best_for: A friendly GUI for local models without the terminal; good for model discovery, testing, and local serving.
strengths: Polished desktop UX; MLX + GGUF; OpenAI-compatible local server; free.
weaknesses: Closed source; heavier than pure CLIs; not a coding agent.
hardware_requirements: Same model-size RAM math as other local runtimes (3Bâ€“8B on 8 GB).

name: GPT4All
official_status_notes: Open-source (MIT) desktop app that runs local LLMs on everyday hardware â€” no GPU or API calls required; LocalDocs for private chat with your files; OpenAI-compatible local API server (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source (MIT), commercial use permitted.
best_for: Private, offline local chat on CPU-only machines; LocalDocs for personal-document Q&A.
weaknesses: Not a coding agent; coding workflows need other tools on top.
hardware_requirements: CPU-only supported; RAM sized to the model you load.

name: Jan
official_status_notes: Open-source (Apache-2.0) offline ChatGPT alternative: local models via llama.cpp, MCP integration, OpenAI-compatible local API (localhost:1337), optional cloud providers (verified Sep 2026).
pricing_summary: Free, open source; cloud providers cost what those providers charge.
best_for: An open-source local AI app with MCP and agent features plus optional cloud providers.
strengths: Apache-2.0; MCP support; OpenAI-compatible local server; cross-platform.
weaknesses: Younger ecosystem than Ollama; the same RAM constraints apply.
hardware_requirements: 8 GB RAM for 3B models, 16 GB for 7B, 32 GB for 13B (per docs).
